written: 2026-10-18 after the pilot (plan section 9 gate), revised after each re-pilot; every entry is a deviation logged in RESULTS.md section 0.1 and plan section 12
stop_why: lever 2: after lever 1 the projection was USD 70.0 (> 50), so the stop is raised to 60 and no arm is dropped for being over 50; lever 3 then applied because 70.0 > 60 (see dropped_arms)
dropped_why: lever 3: projection after levers 1-2 = 70.0 > 60. The costliest open-weight arm by projection among N2 / N3 / N4 / N6 (N1 never; N5 not open-weight at freeze): N2 DeepSeek V4 Pro 13.32 (mean 0.017762 per call over re-pilot 2) against N3 Qwen3.8 13.31 (0.017741) - a near tie of USD 0.01 on three calls each, decided by the rule as written. Projection without N2: 56.7 <= 60, so no further drop. The 5-of-9 rule reads 5-of-8 (three voters + 5 new arms); the P1 open-weight set is N3, N4, N6
reasoning_low_why: lever 1: measured per-call cost exceeded 1.5 x the section-9 line on arms that expose a reasoning parameter: Qwen 0.0878 vs 0.0103 (reasoning 9.5k-17k tokens per call, 267-450 s), Mistral 0.0229 vs 0.0035 (reasoning 9k-11k; one of three calls hit max_tokens 12,000 with no JSON), gpt-oss-120b 0.00045 vs 0.00022 (reasoning ~1.7k), DeepSeek (first served in re-pilot 1, via StreamLake) 0.0221 vs 0.0033 (reasoning 8.2k-11.6k; one of three hit max_tokens with no JSON). Gemini 0.0128 vs 0.0127 did not qualify. reasoning = {effort: low} sent on every call of these arms and recorded per record. Re-pilot 1: Qwen 0.0177 (reasoning 1.7k-2.1k), gpt-oss 0.00027; Mistral unchanged at 0.0204 (reasoning 8.2k-9.7k: the endpoint ignores effort), so Mistral also got the token-cap form below. Re-pilot 2: DeepSeek at effort low 0.0178 (reasoning 5.8k-10.5k, partly honoured)
reasoning_max_tokens_why: lever 1, token-cap form ('where only a token cap is supported'): Mistral's endpoint lists reasoning_effort but re-pilot 1 shows effort low leaves its reasoning at 8.2k-9.7k tokens; reasoning = {max_tokens: 2400} (the budget OpenRouter would derive from effort low at max_tokens 12,000) is sent instead. Re-pilot 2: the budget is ignored too (reasoning 5.8k-8.5k, 0.0180 per call); Mistral runs at its measured cost (13.5 projected) and, not being open-weight at freeze, is outside the lever-3 drop set
thinking_disabled_withdrawn: Attempted as R3-D2 after pilot 1 (the two Claude arms returned reasoning tokens through the gateway, Haiku 649-1,203 per call, Sonnet 509 on one of three, where the direct API of runs 1-2 billed none). Haiku accepted reasoning = {enabled: false} (3 pilot calls, 0 reasoning tokens, USD 0.0004-0.0009 per call, records kept in raw/pilot); the Sonnet endpoint refused every call with 400 'Reasoning is mandatory for this endpoint and cannot be disabled.' Withdrawn for both Claude arms so that they share one regime, which is the frozen plan's 'provider defaults' through the gateway; reasoning tokens are recorded per call and the framing bound (Q5) is read with the caveat that a thinking-regime difference between run 1 and run 3 may be part of it. The judge tries {enabled: false} first and falls back to the default if the Opus endpoint refuses likewise (recorded per record)

transport_retry_R3-D3: After the main run 87 Sonnet 5.5 and 60 Gemini 4 Argon records were transport failures: OpenRouter 429 'Rate limit exceeded: new-account-...' after six attempts with backoff (no model answer was produced; usage null; cost 0). A 429 is not a sample, so these (text, repeat) jobs were re-requested once at concurrency 3 (run_extraction_retry429.log); the failed record stays in the checkpoint file and the served record supersedes it in load_outputs (last record per (text, repeat) wins). Mistral's 89 unparsable outputs (max_tokens 12,000 reached inside the reasoning, finish_reason length) are model outputs and stay failed repeats, never re-sampled

The projection in force (56.7) exceeds the credit, so by the plan's credit-ceiling paragraph (section 9) the run keeps every retained arm and, if the credit runs out, stops checkpointed for the founder to top up and resume; the judge pass starts only if the stop rule allows and stops on its own projection or on exhausted credit
coverage_clause_R3-D4: R3-D4 (logged 2026-10-18 after the run, with ruling R18): the pre-registration coverage clause (plan section 7: a cell with coverage below 50 % of texts, exclusions plus nulls, is uncovered) counted nulls against coverage; written to catch sparse arms, not fields null by design. Applied literally in the frozen scoring (reading (a): every stated-only field uncovered for every arm). R18 adopts reading (b) prospectively - a null-valued answer counts as covered; only invalid outputs and majority exclusions reduce coverage, the run-1 convention under which these fields earned their class - and reading (a) stays reported beside it as the frozen verdict (score.py decision / decision_alt, verdict / verdict_alt; RESULTS.md section 2). Nothing in score.py was changed: the sensitivity column computed before the ruling is the (b) reading
